newsitem.title: ESTONIA: BOURSE TRADE HITS RECORD, KEY BANKS FALL MARKET.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE TRADE HITS RECORD, KEY BANKS FALL MARKET.

text.p: * Total trade at record 184.46 million kroons compared with
the previous record of 178.8 million kroons.
* Index down 1.10 percent to 338.49.
* Hansapank was most traded with 45.85 million
kroons to fall 4.47 kroons to 188.41 kroons.
* Hoiupank falls 4.96 kroons to 191.54 kroons in
trade of 36.9 million kroons.
* Uhispank turnover 41.36 million kroons, up 4.05
kroons to 68.30 kroons.
* On the free market, Norma traded 14.57 million
kroons to lose 0.38 kroons to 87.62 kroons.
Profit-taking knocked down key
banking stocks on the Tallinn bourse on Wednesday as it surged
to record trade, dealers said.
Turnover was a record 184.46 million kroons compared to the
previous peak of 178.8 million kroons set a week ago.
The stock exchange has been exceptionally active for the
last two weeks as the market waits for upward profit forecast
revisions after better than expected interim results.
Foreign investors have also buoyed trade in the wake of the
European Commission's announcement last week that Estonia had
made the grade for the first round of EU entry talks.
But dealers said that Federal Reserve chairman Alan
Greenspan's remarks that U.S. economic growth had moderated had
little to do with the record turnover.
Dealers said continuous profit-taking in Hansapank,
Hoiupank and Forekspank , which climbed to new highs
last week, pulled the index down by 1.10 percent to 338.49.
One dealer said their prices should remain stable for the
rest ahead of the expected upward revision in their profit
forecasts.
Uhispank was higher again by 4.05 kroons to close at 68.30
kroons.
Dealers said it looks like a bargain at its current price.
On the free market, Norma was the most active stock in
trade of 14.57 million kroons to lose 0.38 kroons to 87.62
kroons.
The stock has been active since its parent company sold
some 11.9 percent of its shares to western investors and the
market is also waiting for its revised profit forecast after
strong half-year results, dealers said.
-- Eva Palu, Tallinn newsroom, +372 6209 201,
reuters@reuters.ee
